name: Nairobi & the Mara
tagline: Kenya's vivid capital and the legendary Mara plains.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Aug, Sep, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: July to October for the Great Migration river crossings, January to February for calving and clear skies. Avoid the long rains of April and May.

ourTake.lede: Nairobi is a working city, not a sight to linger over, treat it as the hinge between arrival and the Mara, one or two nights to reset. The move that separates a good trip from an ordinary one is basing inside a private conservancy bordering the reserve rather than the main reserve itself, where you trade shared roads and vehicle jams for off-road driving, night drives and walking. Fly to camp; the road transfer eats a day you don't have.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the definitive African safari, the Migration, private conservancies and camps where the wild comes to your veranda.
ourTake.skipIf: You need city polish and predictability; the Mara is about early mornings, dust and the untamed, not urban comforts.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Angama Mara
items.area: Maasai Mara, Oloololo Escarpment, above the Mara Triangle
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards, No. 1 Resort in Africa
items.description: Two intimate camps of glass-fronted tented suites suspended high on the escarpment, with the whole Mara falling away below, arguably the most cinematic view in Africa.

items.name: Mara Plains Camp
credentials: Relais & Châteaux (member since 2014, Kenya's only Relais & Châteaux)
items.description: Great Plains Conservation's jewel, seven raised tented suites of leather, brass and old-safari romance on the Ntiakitiak River, in a big-cat conservancy off-limits to the crowds.

items.name: Bateleur Camp, &Beyond
items.area: Maasai Mara, Kichwa Tembo concession, western Mara
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards
items.description: 1920s Happy-Valley glamour reborn, swagged canvas, campaign furniture and butler service in a private forest concession beneath the Oloololo Escarpment.

items.name: Cottar's 1920s Camp
items.area: Maasai Mara, Olderkesi Private Conservancy (south-east, bordering the reserve)
credentials: Relais & Châteaux (the only Relais & Châteaux camp bordering the Maasai Mara reserve)
items.description: A fifth-generation family safari and a living time capsule, Persian rugs, steamer trunks and a gramophone that still plays, on its own private conservancy away from every crowd.

items.name: Giraffe Manor
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards, Top Hotels in Africa
items.description: Nairobi's most photographed address, a 1930s ivy-clad manor where the resident Rothschild's giraffes lean their heads through the breakfast windows.

items.name: Sanctuary Olonana
items.area: Maasai Mara, private stretch of the Mara River, within the reserve
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards
items.description: Abercrombie & Kent's riverside lodge, fourteen glass-walled suites over the Mara River, where hippos are the soundtrack and the crossings are minutes away.

items.name: Hemingways Nairobi
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
items.description: A crisp, colonnaded white manor in leafy Karen, 45 suites, a butler to each, and the calmest, most polished city base in Nairobi.

items.name: Sala's Camp
items.area: Maasai Mara, southern reserve, near the Sand and Keekorok rivers
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards
items.description: The Safari Collection's remote southern camp, first light on the Migration as it enters Kenya, and a fire-lit intimacy far from the day-trippers.

items.name: Fairmont The Norfolk
items.description: Kenya's original grand hotel, opened Christmas Day 1904, Tudor gables, the storied Lord Delamere Terrace, and the city that grew up around it.

items.name: Masai Mara Big Five Game Drives
items.description: The Mara is the beating heart of a Kenya safari, open golden savannah studded with acacia and the highest density of big cats anywhere in Africa, where a single morning drive can deliver lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo and, with luck, black rhino. Fly in by light aircraft from Nairobi (about 45 minutes) to a maison-standard tented camp, and your private guide and tracker build the day around the sightings while you never share a vehicle.

items.name: The Great Migration & Mara River Crossings
credentials: Seven Natural Wonders of Africa, the Serengeti–Mara Migration
items.description: From roughly July to October, more than a million wildebeest and zebra pour up from the Serengeti and hurl themselves across the crocodile-filled Mara River in one of the planet's last great wildlife spectacles, chaos, dust and drama at the water's edge. Timing is everything and the finest camps sell out a year ahead, so this is the trip your advisor pins the whole itinerary around.

items.name: Hot-Air Balloon Safari at Dawn over the Mara
items.description: Lift off in the pre-dawn dark and drift in silence a few hundred feet above the plains as the sun comes up and the herds move below you, the single most romantic hour on any African safari, ending with a champagne bush breakfast laid out on white linen in the grass. A bucket-list morning that grandparents and honeymooners remember for the rest of their lives.

items.name: Angama Mara & the Escarpment Camps
items.description: Perched on the rim of the Great Rift Valley with glass-walled tented suites suspended 300 metres above the plains, Angama Mara has the most cinematic view in the Mara, the very ridge where the 'Out of Africa' picnic was filmed. This is the ultra-luxury tier of tented camp, private butlers, veg and Jain menus handled with care, and a swing seat over the endless savannah.

items.name: Mara North Conservancy
items.description: A vast private wilderness bordering the reserve where only a handful of camps share tens of thousands of acres, so a lion sighting is yours alone rather than ringed by twenty vans. Conservancy rules unlock off-road driving right up to the animals, night drives after leopard and aardvark, and guided walking, none of which the main reserve allows.

items.name: Olare Motorogi Conservancy
items.description: 35,000 acres of prime northern Mara with one of the densest lion populations in all of Africa and a strict low-vehicle limit, so exclusivity is written into the model, this is where Richard Branson's Mahali Mzuri sits. For a family that wants the game of the Mara without the crowds, this is the connoisseur's choice.

items.name: Mara Naboisho Conservancy
items.description: One of the largest community-owned conservancies in Africa at roughly 50,000 acres, with rolling hills, leopard-rich thickets and open valleys where cheetah coalitions hunt, and a genuine partnership that puts tourism money directly into Maasai landowners' hands. The walking safaris and night drives here are among the best in Kenya.

items.name: Walking Safari with a Maasai Guide
items.description: Step out of the vehicle and cross the savannah on foot with an armed ranger and a Maasai naturalist, learning to read tracks, dung and birdsong at the pace the bush was meant to be seen, a quiet, intimate counterpoint to the game drive. Only the private conservancies permit it, which is part of why the discerning traveller pays for them.

items.name: Sundowners on the Plains
items.description: The safari day closes with a ritual, your guide parks on a rise as the light turns molten, unpacks a bar from the back of the Land Cruiser, and you toast the day with the whole Mara glowing gold to the horizon. It costs nothing extra and it is, for many, the memory that outlasts the animals.

items.name: A Maasai Village Visit
items.description: A respectful, camp-arranged visit to a manyatta lets you meet the Maasai on their own terms, the jumping dance, fire-making, beadwork and a frank conversation about pastoral life alongside the wildlife. Choose one your camp partners with directly so the money reaches the community rather than a staged roadside show.

items.name: Photographic Safari with a Specialist Guide
items.description: Book a dedicated photographic vehicle, beanbags, a low open-sided rig, a guide who thinks in light and angles and will sit for an hour waiting for the leopard to yawn. For serious hobbyists and multi-gen families with a keen teenager behind the lens, it turns a game drive into a masterclass.

items.name: Nairobi National Park
items.description: The only national park in the world set inside a capital city, lions, giraffe, rhino and buffalo grazing against a backdrop of skyscrapers, minutes from your hotel. A perfect half-day on arrival or before the flight home, and a gentle first taste of the safari for children and grandparents (adult entry around USD 43).

items.name: Sheldrick Wildlife Trust Elephant Orphanage
items.description: The world's most famous orphan-elephant nursery, where rescued calves, many orphaned by poaching or drought, tumble through the mud and take their milk bottles at the one-hour public visit each day (11am, by advance booking only). Deeply moving, endlessly delightful for children, and a chance to foster a calf your family follows for years.

items.name: The Giraffe Centre (AFEW)
items.description: Set up in 1979 by the African Fund for Endangered Wildlife to save the endangered Rothschild's giraffe, this is where you hand-feed the giants from a raised wooden platform, eye to eye. Open daily 9am–5pm, minutes from the Sheldrick Trust, the two make a joyful, easy morning for all ages.

items.name: Breakfast with Giraffes at Giraffe Manor
items.description: The 1930s ivy-clad manor of the Safari Collection, where a resident herd of Rothschild's giraffes pokes its head through the dining-room windows at breakfast for a slice of toast, the most photographed hotel moment in Africa. The twelve rooms book many months ahead and the breakfast is for staying guests only, so it needs planning through your advisor.

items.name: Karen Blixen Museum ('Out of Africa')
items.description: The colonial farmhouse at the foot of the Ngong Hills where the Danish author of 'Out of Africa' lived from 1917, preserved with her furniture and the coffee plantation grounds, the film won seven Oscars and made this hill country legend. A gentle, literary hour open daily, best paired with the Giraffe Centre next door.

items.name: Nairobi National Museum & Snake Park
items.description: The flagship of the National Museums of Kenya, the human-origins hall with fossils from the Rift Valley, superb bird and ethnography galleries, and an adjacent snake park and botanical garden. Two or three cultured hours that give real context before you head to the bush.

items.name: Bomas of Kenya
items.description: A living cultural village recreating the homesteads of Kenya's major communities, with a large auditorium staging spirited traditional song and dance from across the country every afternoon. A colourful, family-friendly window on the cultures behind the wildlife.

items.name: Kazuri Beads Women's Cooperative
items.description: A ceramics workshop founded to employ single mothers, where you watch women hand-roll and glaze the clay beads and pottery sold worldwide, then buy directly from the floor, higher quality and a better story than the markets. A five-minute drive from the Giraffe Centre and a meaningful gift stop.

items.name: Kiambethu Tea Farm
items.description: A working tea estate in the cool green highlands above Nairobi, in the same family since 1910, where a guided walk explains the leaf, a stroll through indigenous forest may turn up colobus monkeys, and lunch is served on the lawn with valley views. A civilised, restful day trip that balances the adrenaline of the safari.

items.name: Ngong Hills Hike
items.description: The knuckled ridge that gives 'Out of Africa' its silhouette, a breezy walk over seven green peaks past a line of wind turbines, with the Rift Valley falling away on one side and the Nairobi skyline on the other. A bracing morning's exercise, best done with a guide, and a fine leg-stretch before or after the bush.

items.name: The Carnivore Restaurant
items.description: A Nairobi institution since 1980, this open-air 'nyama choma' feast roasts endless skewers of meat over a vast charcoal pit and carves them at your table until you lower the paper flag to surrender. A boisterous, only-in-Kenya dinner, and the kitchen will lay on a generous vegetarian spread for those who ask ahead.

items.name: The Maasai Market
items.description: The roving open-air craft market, beadwork, soapstone, wood carvings, kikoi cloth and kanga, that pitches at a different Nairobi location each day of the week (Village Market, the Junction, and more). Go with your guide, haggle gently, and take home the colour of Kenya.

items.name: Nairobi Railway Museum
items.description: The story of the 'Lunatic Line', the railway the British drove from Mombasa to Lake Victoria, and the man-eating lions of Tsavo that stalked its builders, told through vintage locomotives and carriages you can climb aboard. Open daily 8am–5pm; a quiet, atmospheric hour for anyone curious about how modern Kenya was stitched together.

items.name: Amboseli National Park, Elephants beneath Kilimanjaro
items.description: The classic postcard of Africa: great herds of elephant crossing the dust with the snows of Kilimanjaro floating above them, Amboseli's flat, open floor gives the finest elephant viewing and the most famous mountain backdrop in Kenya. An easy light-aircraft hop and a natural pairing with the Mara for a two-park safari.

items.name: Lake Nakuru National Park, Flamingos & Rhinos
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Kenya Lake System in the Great Rift Valley
items.description: A shimmering soda lake famous for its pink drifts of flamingo and, more reliably now, one of Kenya's best places to see both black and white rhino, plus tree-climbing lions and Rothschild's giraffe. Part of the UNESCO-listed Kenya Lake System, and an easy addition to a Rift Valley loop.

items.name: Lake Bogoria & Lake Elementaita
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Kenya Lake System in the Great Rift Valley
items.description: Bogoria's steaming hot springs and geysers draw vast congregations of lesser flamingo, while quieter Elementaita completes the trio of alkaline lakes that hold up to four million birds between them. Together with Nakuru they form the UNESCO Kenya Lake System, a birder's and geologist's dream a couple of hours from Naivasha.

items.name: Lake Naivasha Boat Safari
items.description: A freshwater Rift Valley lake where a small boat glides you among hippo pods and past fish eagles snatching prey from the surface, gentle, scenic and a lovely change of tempo from the game drive. The lakeshore lodges make a relaxed base for exploring Hell's Gate and Crescent Island next door.

items.name: Crescent Island Walking Safari
items.description: A private sanctuary with no predators, so you can walk freely on foot among giraffe, zebra, eland, waterbuck and wildebeest, a rare, safe, unhurried way to be at eye level with plains game. Reached by a short boat ride across Naivasha and perfect for children old enough to walk a few kilometres.

items.name: Hell's Gate National Park by Bike
items.description: One of the very few Kenyan parks you can explore on a bicycle or on foot, cycling among zebra and giraffe between towering red cliffs and gorges, the landscape that inspired 'The Lion King'. An active, exhilarating half-day for families with teenagers who need to burn energy.

items.name: Samburu National Reserve, the Northern Specials
items.description: A rugged, arid reserve on the Ewaso Ng'iro river where you find species seen almost nowhere else on a Kenya safari, Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, the long-necked gerenuk and beisa oryx, alongside big cats and elephant. The starkly beautiful, less-trodden north for travellers who have already done the Mara.

items.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy, the Last Northern White Rhinos
items.description: The 360-square-kilometre conservancy that guards Najin and Fatu, the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, under armed round-the-clock protection, a chance to stand with a species at the very edge of existence. Also East Africa's largest black-rhino sanctuary and a genuinely purpose-driven place to bring children.

items.name: Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary
items.description: The only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees, a Jane Goodall Institute sanctuary within Ol Pejeta that gives lifelong refuge to apes rescued from the illegal trade across Central and West Africa. A moving, educational stop that pairs naturally with the rhino experience.

items.name: Lewa Wildlife Conservancy
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, extension of Mount Kenya National Park / Natural Forest
items.description: A pioneering private conservancy that holds a significant share of Kenya's rhino and, with the neighbouring Ngare Ndare forest, forms an official extension of the Mount Kenya UNESCO World Heritage Site. Horseback safaris, superb rhino viewing and a conservation model the world studies, the thinking traveller's safari.

items.name: Laikipia Plateau Private Ranches
items.description: A high, wild plateau of vast private conservancies and family-run ranches where the safari turns creative, horseback and camel treks, mountain-biking, fly-camping and night drives that the national parks never allow. Sparse, exclusive and endlessly varied, it is where repeat Kenya travellers go for something new.

items.name: Mount Kenya National Park
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Mount Kenya National Park / Natural Forest
items.description: Africa's second-highest peak, its glacier-hung summit and afro-alpine moorland rising straight from the equator, you can trek the scenic Chogoria or Sirimon routes to the trekker's summit of Point Lenana over several days. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a serious highland adventure to bolt onto a classic safari.

items.name: Tsavo East & Tsavo West, the Red Elephants
items.description: Kenya's largest wilderness, bigger than some countries, where elephants dust themselves in the brick-red iron soil and glow terracotta, and Mzima Springs runs crystal-clear among hippo and crocodile. Raw, vast and uncrowded, and the natural bridge between a Nairobi safari and the Indian Ocean coast.

items.name: Diani Beach, Bush & Beach
items.description: Powder-white sand and warm turquoise water on the palm-fringed south coast, the classic way to end a Kenya safari, swap the Land Cruiser for a dhow, a spa and a lounger. Just up from Tsavo, it makes the effortless bush-and-beach combination that Indian families love for the multi-generational reward at the end.

items.name: Watamu & the Marine National Parks
items.description: A quieter coral-coast alternative to Diani, with a protected marine park for snorkelling and diving over reefs, a turtle-watch programme, and the mangrove creeks of Mida, plus the atmospheric Gede ruins nearby. Bush-and-beach with a gentler, more natural rhythm.

items.name: Private Conservancy Night Game Drives
items.description: After dark, a red-filtered spotlight reveals a whole second Africa the daytime hides, hunting leopard, aardvark, bat-eared fox, genet and the eyes of a lion on the move. Available only on the private conservancies, it is one of the clearest reasons to pay for that exclusivity.

items.name: Conservation & Anti-Poaching Experiences
items.description: Many top camps let guests spend a morning with the people doing the work, tracking rhino on foot with the monitoring team, meeting the canine anti-poaching unit, or joining a research drive. A purposeful, behind-the-scenes half-day that turns a luxury holiday into something the whole family carries home.

items.name: Light-Aircraft Safari Transfers
items.description: The way discerning travellers move around Kenya, a scheduled or private Cessna from Nairobi's Wilson Airport hops you to a Mara or Amboseli airstrip in under an hour, over the Rift Valley and the herds, sparing hours of rough road. Book the private charter for total flexibility on timing and camps.

items.name: Governors' Camp & Little Governors'
items.description: The grande dame of Mara camps, sitting on a prime bend of the Mara River inside the reserve where the migration crosses right in front of the tents, run with old-world safari polish for generations. For travellers who want the classic reserve position and heritage rather than a conservancy, this is the benchmark.

items.name: Mahali Mzuri
items.description: Richard Branson's twelve-tent camp in the lion-rich Olare Motorogi conservancy, pod-like suites tumbling down a hillside above a wildlife corridor, all game drives, walks and night drives included, with a spa and impeccable service. The polished, design-forward end of the Mara for a couple or a family seeking privacy.

items.name: Chyulu Hills & the Kilimanjaro Foothills
items.description: The rolling green volcanic hills Hemingway called the 'Green Hills of Africa', where private wilderness camps offer horseback and walking safaris in the shadow of Kilimanjaro on Maasai-owned land. A serene, low-density extension for those who have seen the headline parks and want the road less travelled.

items.name: Talisman
items.description: Nairobi's most-loved restaurant, a rambling colonial house in Karen, oriental rugs and fireplaces, and an East-African-meets-global menu that has defined city dining for two decades.

items.name: INTI
items.description: Nikkei cooking, Japanese precision married to Peruvian fire, from a rooftop with the Nairobi skyline laid out below, and a Pisco Sour to match.

items.name: Cultiva
items.area: Naivasha (day trip from Nairobi / en route to the Rift)
items.description: A farm-to-table kitchen in a lakeside garden, much of the menu grown on the property, and one of Kenya's most talked-about dining rooms.

items.name: Lord Delamere Terrace
items.description: Breakfast, lunch or a sundowner on the terrace that has watched Nairobi go by since 1904, the city's most storied place to sit and take it in.

items.name: The Carnivore
credentials: Ranked No. 47, World's Best 50 Restaurants (2003), a Nairobi icon
items.description: The great Nairobi institution, an open-air 'beast of a feast' where skewers of roast meats are carved at your table until you lower the paper flag.

items.name: Nyama Mama
credentials: Notable Nairobi venue, Kenyan comfort food, widely recognised
items.description: A bright, playful 'modern African diner' reinventing Kenyan home cooking, ugali, nyama and coastal Swahili plates with colour and wit.

items.name: Bush sundowners & the campfire
credentials: The signature evening ritual of every Mara lodge
items.description: The Mara's true nightlife, a drink poured on a rise as the sun drops behind the escarpment, then dinner and stories around the fire under the biggest sky you'll ever see.

items.name: Lord Delamere Terrace & Bar
items.description: A sundowner on the 1904 terrace where every explorer, settler and safari-goer has raised a glass, the most historic drink in Kenya.

items.name: Giraffe Manor drawing room
items.description: An evening drink by the fire in the ivy-clad manor, giraffes wandering the lawn outside the leaded windows, a private, storybook nightcap.

items.name: INTI Rooftop
items.description: Nairobi's most stylish rooftop, Pisco Sours and Nikkei small plates over the city lights, from a bar team as serious as the kitchen.

plan.heading: 6 days in Nairobi & the Mara, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into Hemingways Nairobi in Karen, then a quiet late breakfast on the terrace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Private visit to the Giraffe Centre and the David Sheldrick elephant orphanage, arranged for the calm hour before the crowds.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Talisman in Karen, unhurried, with a table booked in the garden room.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Karen Blixen's farmhouse and the Ngong foothills, then coffee at a working estate above the city.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Nairobi National Museum with a curator, followed by an hour among the beadwork at Kazuri.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Chef's table dinner at Cultiva or a quiet evening at the hotel before the early flight.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Light-aircraft transfer from Wilson to an airstrip in the Mara Triangle, met by your guide.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Settle into Angama Mara on the escarpment, then an unhurried first game drive as the plains fill.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners at the edge of the Rift, dinner brought to the deck under the stars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Dawn drive in the private Mara Triangle, following the guide's read of the light and the herds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Rest through the heat, lunch overlooking the plains, then a slow afternoon on the river.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Bush dinner laid out by the camp, lanterns and a fire, guides telling the day back to you.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Full-day drive with a packed breakfast, tracking the Mara River crossings if the season allows.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A quiet lunch in the shade, then time to simply watch, no schedule, just the plains.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Private dinner on the Out of Africa kopje, the whole valley below you.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A final dawn drive, unhurried, then breakfast as the balloons lift over the plains.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Light-aircraft transfer back to Nairobi, day room held at Hemingways to freshen up.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Early supper and a discreet transfer to Jomo Kenyatta for the night flight home.

items.name: Karen
items.description: Leafy, colonial-era estates near the giraffe centre and Karen Blixen house, calm, green, best for a soft first night.

items.name: Mara North Conservancy
items.description: Private land on the reserve's edge; low vehicle density and off-road access, for travellers who want exclusivity over price.

items.name: Gigiri
items.description: The diplomatic quarter near the UN, secure, quiet and convenient to the airport for a functional stopover.

events.name: Great Wildebeest Migration river crossings
events.note: Peak crossing season in the Mara; the exact days are unpredictable, so allow several nights and book camps 12-18 months ahead.

events.name: WRC Safari Rally Kenya
events.note: The historic World Rally round runs on the rough tracks around Lake Naivasha, a couple of hours from Nairobi.

events.name: Lamu Cultural Festival
events.note: Dhow races, poetry and Swahili weddings on the coastal island, a natural add-on if you extend beyond the safari.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Choose a private conservancy (Mara North, Naboisho, Olare Motorogi) over the reserve itself for exclusivity, night drives and off-road access; July falls in the Great Migration window, and evenings at altitude are cold, so pack a layer.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Land at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International (NBO), overnight at Hemingways or Giraffe Manor, then fly into the Mara by light aircraft from Wilson Airport to a private airstrip where your camp's ranger meets you.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: In the Mara you move by open 4x4 with a dedicated guide and tracker; in Nairobi a private chauffeur is standard given traffic and distance.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Safaricom eSIM covers Nairobi and most Mara camps well; deep-bush conservancies rely on camp Wi-Fi and Starlink, so treat true off-grid stretches as intentional.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Kenyan shilling (KES); US dollars are widely accepted for park fees and camps, cards work in Nairobi, and guides/camp staff appreciate discreet USD tips.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Dry season July-October is the reliable window: clear plains, thinned vegetation and the wildebeest river crossings; skip the long rains of April-May when tracks flood and camps thin out.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Kenya Airways flies Mumbai-Nairobi nonstop in about 6h30m; from Delhi and Bengaluru it is one stop via Mumbai or a Gulf hub (Emirates, Qatar) in J. Nairobi is the connection point for the light-aircraft hop into the Mara, so allow a comfortable overnight rather than a same-day tag-on to the bush camp.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Yellow fever certificate is required for onward Tanzania and often checked; malaria prophylaxis for the Mara, and routine vaccines current. Nairobi warrants city sense after dark; the private conservancies are secure. Drink bottled or filtered water.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian and Jain are well understood; the top Mara camps cater to both with notice, and Nairobi has real Indian cooking. Consider a night at Chowpaty or Haandi in Nairobi before flying into camp.
